newsitem.title: USA: GM releases separate results for Delphi.
newsitem.headline: GM releases separate results for Delphi.

text.p: General Motors Corp Wednesday released separate financial results for its Delphi Automotive Systems unit for the first time.
Following is a summary of Delphi's annual financial results for the years 1994, 1995 and 1996 ($ in Millions).

NOTE: Delphi 1996 net includes charge of $153 million for sale of facilities, plus $49 million charge for retiree lump-sum payments. Excluding extraordinary charges, Delphi net income was $728 million for 1996, $916 million for 1995 and $686 million for 1994.
GM North American Operations excluding Delphi

NOTE: 1996 NAO net includes net gain of $397 million -- including $450 million gain from plant closing reserve adjustment, a $65 million gain from sale of preferred stock interest, a charge of $114 million from retiree lump sum payments and a charge of $4 million for sale of facilities.
Excluding extraordinary items, GM's NAO unit would have earned $333 million in 1996, $1,524 in 1995 and $706 million in 1994.

Combined NAO and Delphi net income was $1.246 billion in 1996, $2.396 billion in 1995 and $677 million in 1994. GM attributes the decline in both NAO and Delphi 1996 results to U.S. and Canadian strikes that curtailed production and to North American model changeovers.
